preamble: The aspirated retroflex affricate [ʈʂʰ] (pinyin ch) merges with the aspirated alveolar affricate [tsʰ] (pinyin c) in several Mandarin varieties. In Taiwanese Mandarin the deretroflexion is a pervasive feature of everyday speech, attributed to Southern Min substrate influence; in Southwestern Mandarin (e.g. Chengdu) the retroflex series is entirely absent, so words with Standard Mandarin ch- regularly have tsʰ-. The change is part of a series-wide merger affecting zh, ch and sh together.

examples.note: Retroflex initials zh, ch, sh merge into z, c, s in most Taiwan Mandarin speech, including that of highly educated speakers; producing retroflexes is regarded as a marker of 'good' Guoyu and triggers hypercorrection.
Sichuanese lacks the retroflex initials [tʂ tʂʰ ʂ ʐ] of Beijing Mandarin; the whole series corresponds to dental sibilants.
